utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. President. Case IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good morning to you. Mr. Oric, good morning to you, too. Can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Patricia Sellers of the Prosecution. I'm accompanied by co-counsel, Ms. Joanne Richardson, and our case manager is Donnica Henry-Frijlink. Good morning to Defence counsel also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to my learned friends and colleagues from the OTP. I'm Vasvija Vidovic. Together with Mr. John Jones, I appear for Mr. Naser Oric. We have with us our legal assistant, Ms. Jasmina Cosic, and our case manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good morning to you, too. Now, any preliminaries before we bring in the witness? I see none. Usher, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, madam.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome, once more. Please take a seat, and we will proceed with your testimony. Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Radovic. I would like to resume my questioning concerning your arrival in Srebrenica, and I believe you testified that you arrived with four of the other persons who were prisoners from Cerska, and brought by Mr. Zulfo Tursunovic and two other armed and camouflaged men. I would like to ask you, when you arrived in Srebrenica, did you immediately go and register your names with any agency?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First they brought us to a room. Two men beat us there, especially the three men. And then later, in the evening, and at night, a man took me to the women's room and he took them to the men's room.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Well, when you were in the room where the people beat yourself and the other men, could you please tell me what clothes, if any, were the men who beat you wearing?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Black uniform and black shades.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were any of the men wearing camouflage uniforms or civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Srebrenica, you mean, or my men --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, I'm talking about the men you met when you came to Srebrenica, in that room where you were beat.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, was Zulfo Tursunovic and the other two men who had escorted you from Cerska, were they in the room while you were beat?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you please describe for the Trial Chamber the type of beating that you received and the type of beating that the other men - I imagine you're referring to Jakov Dzokic, Mr. Ilic - received in the room also.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in this room where they brought us or in the prison in general?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, I'm talking about in the room where they brought you when you first arrived. The other person would be Rado Pejic, excuse me. What type of beating was administered in that room when you first arrived?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other person, Rado Pejic, they kicked him and slapped him. His head was bleeding because he had banged his head against a cupboard.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did Zulfo Tursunovic return to the room where he had left the four of you?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did he make any remark concerning the physical appearance of yourself or of the other men he left with you, the imprisoned men?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He showed aggression against those two uniformed men.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Was he mad that they had beaten you?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, when he saw those men bleeding.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, when you say "he saw those men bleeding," are you referring to Mr. Pejic, Mr. Ilic?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dzokic too.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And Mr. Dzokic. So it's your testimony that Mr. Tursunovic visibly saw injuries, and then was mad at the men in uniform --

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: -- who administered them. Now, just to recap a bit, when you arrived in Srebrenica, you stated that it was the evening; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And also, you stated -- you testified prior that it was the 26th of January, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to show the witness an exhibit that's priorly been marked P15.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Ms. Radovic, I'd ask you to look at the document that's in front of you. And would you just confirm for the Trial Chamber that the date at the top of that document corresponds to the date that you arrived in the Srebrenica prison? I'm sorry, corresponds to when you arrived in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here the 9th of January, 1993, and that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could I see the document that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, this is not the correct document. Your Honours, could you give me one minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, for clarity's sake, it's part of P15. It would be ERN 01239555. Could we please show that to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 26th of January, 1993, that is the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And would you also look below where it says "hour," and it says between 1400 and 2200. Would you agree that you arrived in Srebrenica between 1400 hours and 2200 hours?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We arrived in the evening. It was dark. I cannot remember the exact time. I did not have a watch. But it was dark, and there were already lights on, so we couldn't really distinguish anything when they brought us into the prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, would you look at that document where it says number 1, and next to it, it says "Dzokic." Is this the person who you were referring to, who you were in the stable with, who you walked between Cerska and Srebrenica with, and was now with you in the room when the beating was administered?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jakov Dzokic. That evening, he was not in the prison with me, but he had been with me in the stable. He had been taken to the men's room. We heard him moan outside the door. Someone told me, You're no longer going to be helping the army. But we could only hear very little of what was going on because the door was closed, and we were in the women's room.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you look at the person's name next to number 2. It says "Ilic." Is this the Ilic who you were in prison with in Cerska and who came down to Srebrenica with you on the 26th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Dragan Ilic, son of Ljubinko.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'd also ask you to look at number 3. Is this the same Pejic that you testified about who was in prison with you in Cerska, who came down to Srebrenica with you on the 26th of January of 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rade Pejic, yes, he came with me, or rather, with us to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And number 4, does that person refer to you, that name?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Radovic, had you transferred or given any information concerning your date of birth, where you had lived, where you had originally been captured, to Zulfo Tursunovic any time from his arrival in Cerska to your arrival in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I provided information in Bajrici when they captured me and brought me to that room. I gave them all my personal information, as well as details stated on my ID.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And the night that you arrived, is it your testimony that you did not personally give any information to someone whose name is Fahrudin Delic, the name you see at the bottom of this document.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The next morning, they took me away. I can't remember the man's name, but they took me away the next morning. I told them whatever I told them, and he then said, You are free to go. He treated me in a fair manner, and it was a brief thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm finished with this document at the moment. It's already been marked and is an exhibit. I'd also like to be able to tender the complete English translations of the document. I believe people have the first page. Co-counsel, Gramsci Di Fazio, I believe, might have used the document, but we were not able at that point in time to hand up the complete English translations.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Radovic. After...

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: After Zulfo Tursunovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And this was P15 -- was it P15?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: P15, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Ms. Radovic, after Zulfo Tursunovic came back to the room where you had been held and where there was a beating, did he then take you and the other males to another building or another location?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That man was taken out and then someone else was brought along. But it was dark, so we couldn't see. They were taken as far as the door to the rooms.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could you please describe the other building that you were taken to, and whether you met other prisoners there.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only describe across the way, I didn't see a single prisoner. I only went into a single room where the man was. I didn't know his name. The name was stated there, but I didn't see any other prisoners there --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, I'm referring to the previous night, the night of the 26th, when you testified that Zulfo Tursunovic took you and the other men to another building.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm not sure if she actually did say that Zulfo Tursunovic took her to a building, or it's not even clear yet that she had been taken to the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'll withdraw that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you're right, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If my friend could lead as little as possible at this stage when we come to the prison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly. I'm sure Ms. Sellers knows how to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Ms. Radovic, you testified that you were in a room with the other male prisoners where they were beaten up, and afterwards you testified that Mr. Zulfo Tursunovic came back to that room and that he appeared angry to the men who had beaten you up. My question now is: Did you, Mr. Ilic, Mr. Dzokic, and also Mr. Pejic, were you then taken from that room and taken to another place in Srebrenica that night?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That night we were taken to the prison only. I was placed in the women's room and they were placed in the men's room.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you please describe what the women's room in the prison looked like.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The room was quite high. The windows were very large. It was cold in it. There were a number of women there. We slept on the floor. We only had one blanket to go around, to lie on and to protect ourselves with. We had some timber from a barrel, but we didn't have a stove to make a fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, you stated that you were taken to this building. Could you please tell the Trial Chamber, who took you or escorted you to this building where the women were in the prison?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zulfo took us outside that other room, and then I don't know who it was that took us over, in a manner of speaking, because it was nighttime.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, in this other building where you met the other women, was it your impression that these women were imprisoned?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were you placed in a room where the door was locked? Or was the door open and you had free access to go in or out of the room?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The door was not locked, but the door was locked from our side. We couldn't leave. They, on the other hand, could go in and out as they pleased.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, when you referred to "they," could you tell the Trial Chamber who "they" were?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those guards who were on duty, and whoever else wanted to come in.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, the guards on duty, could you tell the Trial Chamber whether they were dressed in a uniform or whether they were wearing civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And was their uniform similar to the uniform that Zulfo Tursunovic was wearing or the other men who escorted you from Cerska?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those guards who were there had no insignia on their sleeves, or armbands.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber, if you remember, how many guards were outside of the door where the women were?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They all sat across the way in the corridor outside our room. They were usually two -- there were usually two a shift, but I couldn't be sure because we weren't allowed to go out and look.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, inside the room where the women who you had the impression were imprisoned, did you have the ability to learn the names of at least some of those female prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Please tell the Trial Chamber, if you remember, the names of the female prisoners.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dostana Filipovic, from Bjelovac. Milka Tomic from a place near Bratunac. Milisava Nikolic from Kravica. There were two women named Milena from Skelani. Zivana, with a daughter Svetlana, nicknamed Svetsa. There was Zeljko there too. But the women slept in the house and not with us. Mira Filipovic, Dostana's sister-in-law, she lived in the house with two small children; Olivera was three, and Nemanja was six months old. There was an old women named Danica and Aunt Stojanka. I called her Stojanka, but I never saw those women. I went to visit Dostana in the hospital. She died, and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the last name of the person who stayed alive and is from Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could you please state the name of the person who was from Kravica, who stayed alive?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milisava Nikolic, from Kravica, she survived, but her nerves were damaged badly. Dostana Filipovic, from Bjelovac, on the other hand, died.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction: It should read the boys lived in the house, not the women lived in the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber, during your stay at the prison, was there enough room for the women to lie down and sleep in that room?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, there was enough room on the floor. I can't say otherwise. We had an agreement to put two blankets on the floor so that we wouldn't be cold, and then three of us would sleep on those two blankets and cover ourselves with the third blanket so as not to be cold.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And were you also given food on a daily basis while you were in the prison?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would receive food in the evening and in the morning, in the course of 24 hours. We would receive food regularly in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: While you were in the prison in Srebrenica, were you ever beaten or physically assaulted?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was slapped twice by one man, but I cannot remember any other details about him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you, at times, receive visits from people, such as Muslim women, while you were in the prison?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They used to come, two girls, whose names I don't know. When we went to be exchanged, they stayed quite a long time with us. They bid us goodbye, very properly. We said goodbye to them. They wanted to move to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So would it be your testimony that, although conditions were very bad, that while you were at the prison in Srebrenica, the women did not suffer any physical attacks but just endured the hardship in terms of the limited space and limited food?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I hate to object, but the witness never said the conditions were very bad, she never said anything about hardships. Again, this inference on my learned friend's --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: You're right, that might be characterisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Objection sustained. Rephrase your question, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Ms. Radovic, would you agree that during your time period in the gaol in Srebrenica, the prison in Srebrenica, that although your food was limited to once a day, I believe your testimony --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Twice a day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: -- twice a day, and that you slept on the ground with three on a blanket, but that you were never assaulted or otherwise physically injured while in the prison. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not assaulted. I was slapped only twice. As for the other women who I found there in prison, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you about the men who came with you from Cerska. Do you know whether they were placed in the same building or not?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the same building, but they would take a different hallway or they would go straight through the hallway, whereas I was right across from the hallway.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you know approximately how far away they were from the women's room in that same building?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, two and a half to 3 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were you able to hear them in the room that you were in with the other women?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you ever hear what appeared to be, from your point of view, sounds of suffering or sounds that implied infliction of pain?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We heard moans, but we couldn't tell who moaned, we couldn't recognise the voices.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you know whether the moans were coming from male prisoners or coming from people who were not imprisoned in the building?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most likely from the prisoners. Nobody else could have come in.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you ever hear any names, or something that would give you the impression that you might have known one of the prisoners who was moaning?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I told you that I heard when they beat Jakov, asking him, Well, whose army are you going to serve now, whose army are you going to serve in now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you know whether the beatings took place where the men were held or whether they took place in the corridor or some other place in the building?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several times we heard in front of our door, but we couldn't see anything, because we couldn't see through the door.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And could you tell the Trial Chamber what it is that you heard near the door?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Moans, as I told you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, would you hear this on a frequent basis, on a daily basis, or was this only occasional, once or twice during your stay?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every other night.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: How long a period of time would you estimate that you heard these sounds, the moans?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in terms of the time, I couldn't really tell you. I didn't have my watch. But it could be around one hour or 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: You've testified that you spoke to other persons on forms of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would like to now show another Prosecution exhibit, but I will need to ask for a number for this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Ms. Radovic, I'd ask you to look at the document, please. When you were taken to be asked questions during your stay at the Srebrenica prison --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just don't recall the witness saying she was taken for questioning when she was in Srebrenica prison. It's being suggested to her. I can check the transcript, but I just don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe she did say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think she did say at one point in time she was asked questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: From the prison, I'm not sure. I'll have a look. If not, it's a suggestion on my learned friend's part.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Well, let me ask.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were you ever taken, while you were staying at the Srebrenica prison, for questioning?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once, as I told you, on the second day after my arrival.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And when you were taken for questioning, were you treated --

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the morning, at around 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: -- were you treated respectfully?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And the person who asked you questions, was that person wearing a uniform other was that person dressed in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uniformed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And was that the same uniform or the similar uniform to that worn by the guards or Zulfo Tursunovic or the men who escorted you to the prison?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person in civilian clothes --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't understand what the witness said. Could she please repeat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Radovic, the interpreters could not hear what you were saying. Could you please repeat your answer. They only heard you say "The person in civilian clothes ..." Let me repeat the question to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know Ivanka, and the rest of it is correct. I don't know for the bottom part of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You were asked the following question: "The person who asked you questions, was that person wearing a uniform or was that person dressed in civilian clothes?" And you answered "Uniformed." "And was that the same uniform or the similar uniform to that worn by the guards of Zulfo Tursunovic or the men who escorted you to the prison." And you had started answering that question. I would like you to answer that question. In other words, you are being asked whether that was the same uniform or a similar uniform to that worn by the guards of Zulfo Tursunovic or the men who escorted you to the prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was in a uniform. I think that the uniform was blue, although my recollection is not the best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Ms. Radovic, the person who asked you questions, did he ask you questions where you were able to confirm information, such as, were you arrested on a certain date?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did it appear that he already knew something about the circumstances of your arrest and prior detention?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He most likely had the papers. He received them when we arrived, at night.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the rest of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could you just speak up a bit. The interpreter wasn't able to hear the last part of the answer. You said, "He received them when we arrived, at night," and then you were continuing.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when he took us from Cerska, he most likely took our papers for Srebrenica, and most likely turned them over to that man either that evening or the following day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. And you would just confirm that the paper that you had in front of you --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could I ask the usher to please hand it back.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: -- that what is written under your name coincides with the information that you gave him or that he had about you.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These -- I gave this information, and it's all correct. But I don't know for the upper portion of what is written in this document. I don't know Ivanka Mitrovic. I don't know this lady.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't blame you for getting confused on that, because it shouldn't have been given to us, it shouldn't have been translated in the first place, or it at least shouldn't have appeared on this document in any case. Don't worry about it, Madam Radovic, that that happens to be there, because in the original, the two persons were dealt with on the same page and therefore the translators translated the entire page and did not limit themselves to what was written about you. So don't worry about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Ms. Radovic, I just want to ask you one further question about this document. In it, the document states that you were at your job, at the Vezionica. Isn't it true that at the time that you were arrested, that you had stopped working at your job due to the blockades that you testified about earlier?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I stopped going to work and then they called me to go and work. And we went across the Drina to Mali Zvornik, to Karakaj. We went in a boat. I mentioned that. And if you don't believe me, you can ask Kadrija because everybody saw me that night when I came to fetch my clothes. You can call everybody in the village and ask them. There's nothing for me to be ashamed about, because I have spoken only the truth. And I have said that I only want to say the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would ask that this document be admitted into evidence and receive a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, registrar, this will be 4 ...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 491.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: For the record, we object to the authenticity of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Ms. Guibert, please make a note of that so that when we come later to the question of objections, we will have a complete record.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like the witness to be shown what has been referred to as P19. I believe it's currently in Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Ms. Radovic, you testified that there were male prisoners or men in the prison, and you knew some of their names, and also you testified about the names of some of the female prisoners. I would like you to look at the document in front of you, and would you look at number 10 on the document.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you agree that that refers to you and how you came to the detention centre in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you please look at number 17 on the list.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you also agree that that refers to the Rado Pejic that you have referred to, and that that is how he came to the detention centre in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you please look at number 1 on the list.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could you also confirm the typewritten information there?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And also, number 2 on the list that refers to Branko Sekulic, could you confirm the typewritten information?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, do you see other people's names on the list who were with you in the Srebrenica prison?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that you didn't mention Dragan Ilic, number 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you confirm that that information is correct concerning him?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Dragan Ilic, the information is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you recognise other names on that list?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Filipovic Dostana.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And would you also confirm that the information concerning her is correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Ilija was there. He used to bring in firewood for us. He was disturbed. Milisava, but it says Milanovic, not Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: You're now referring to number 8 on the list. And priorly, did you refer to number 7 on the list, as Ilija?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivanovic, Ilija, son of Radenko, was exchanged together with me. He used to bring in firewood for us, into the prison. I don't know where he was from, but I know that he used to come into our women's room and bring in firewood.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So would you confirm, then, that information that's given under number 7?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will ask that the document be taken from the witness at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Ms. Sellers, the document is dated the 3rd of February, 1993. Now, if you go to number 17, it gives some information on March 17.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: -- Three months later. How can it --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: We're in the situation where the document that we have in translation in English is completely typewritten. The original document that the witness is using, and it might be illustrative to show that, the information that post-dates the 3rd of February is handwritten. It is now on Sanction, Your Honour. You can see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Do you need this document any further? I heard you say you don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: We don't need the document any further. I'm going to ask a couple of clarifying questions, but the document can be removed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Ms. Radovic, would you please tell the Trial Chamber the date you arrived at the Srebrenica prison and the date that you left the Srebrenica prison.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 26th of January, 1993. The agreement was signed on the 5th of February, 1993. We were exchanged on the 6th of February, 1993, in Veznik, in Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So the information that we saw on that document, that you confirmed as being correct to the Trial Chamber, is that information that you're knowledgable about between the 26th of January, 1993 and the 6th of February, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to turn your attention back to the prison and ask you: Did you know who was in charge of the prison?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Had you ever heard anyone's name being given as being the authority in the prison?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And did you ever see anyone come to the women's cell in the prison and say that they were in a position of authority?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did anyone ever tell you who might be in a position of authority?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you about the time period leading up to your exchange, or to when you left the prison. You just testified that on the 5th of February, an agreement was reached. Tell the Trial Chamber what agreement you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the agreement on exchange was signed. Gedza informed us about this. I think he was from Srebrenica. He came one evening and said, Hey, are you celebrating, women? You are to be exchanged tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, this person you've mentioned as Gedza, could you tell the Trial Chamber, did he say this personally to the women?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he came into our room and told us that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber how he was dressed?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in uniform, but he always treated us respectfully and fairly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Was he one of the guards, or did he work in any other capacity in the prison section?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so, I don't think he was a guard. I don't know, though, whether he had some other role.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, on the day that he announced that you would be exchanged, were you able to visit any of the men in the prison?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: That evening, prior to the exchange, were you able to visit any of the men that had come with you from Cerska?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you ever see Branko Sekulic, Rado Pejic, Dragan Ilic, or Jakov Dzokic prior to your leaving the prison in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked Gedza, rather, I asked him whether I could go in and say goodbye to them. I went into the room, and that was it. Later on, I saw Rado when he was set free.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Well, when you went into the room, would you tell the Trial Chamber, how did those men look, physically, to you?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Terrible. They were black and blue, all swollen up. I got scared when I saw them, because when we had arrived, they didn't look that way. Therefore, I really got stared when I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did Rado Pejic look as if he had been black and bruisened?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And also, did Branko Sekulic look as if he had been black and bruisened?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could you also state the same for Mr. Dzokic?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And would that also be true for Dragan Ilic?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, that night you were able to say goodbye to them, how close were you standing from those men?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in the morning, that wasn't at night. We stood perhaps a metre from each other. We simply extended our hands for a handshake.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So you were able to physically touch them; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I mean we shook hands.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And were you able to see them clearly, even though your eye had been injured previously?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was able to see them. I had spent a long time with them. I was very scared because they were really in bad shape, badly beaten.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And then were you taken back to the women's cell?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Where were you taken to next?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took us outside the prison. There was some sort of a green kiosk outside. We waited for a lorry, and then a van came. But the ignition didn't work so a lorry came. There were people there, locals, who were spitting at us; some were just silent. And then we were picked up, loaded onto a lorry, and then we were off to Veznik, to wait for our Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. exchange.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: When you say that there were locals who were spitting at you, are you referring to people who were Bosnian Muslims or Bosnian Serbs or another ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were they saying anything to you when they were spitting at you?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were saying things but I forgot all about myself at that time. I was not really fully aware of what was going on, because I thought we weren't being taken to an exchange. My suspicion is that we would soon meet our end, all of a sudden.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: By that, do you mean that you thought that it was possible that you were being taken to be killed?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were all convinced about it. We weren't thinking anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, did any of the men in camouflage who were at the prison accompany you to the exchange?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three men came, Zulfo and two other men. I don't know their names. They handed us over to our forces. They carried lists with the names of people to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And was it after that time period that you entered back into Bosnian Serb territory and were no longer a prisoner?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we came to Veznik, when we were being exchanged, I was no longer a prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you ever have the chance to see Rado Pejic after your exchange?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him when he arrived at the hospital. He called me and I came over for a visit. It was in the Zvornik Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: When you saw Rado Pejic, could you tell the Trial Chamber what he physically looked like at that time?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in a bad shape. He was unable to walk. He told me and the police officers that SFOR had brought him there. He was in a very bad shape. When I left detention, I weighed 37 kilos myself, and I simply couldn't believe that I would survive.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you remember what month and what year it was that you saw Rado Pejic?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in 1993, but I can't give you the month.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you ask him about the other men who had stayed in the stable with you in Cerska? Branko Sekulic?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I asked him what had become of Branko, Dragan, and Jakov, and he just told me, They all met a tragic end, they succumbed to the beatings. That was all he said. We couldn't say anything more because we felt so bad. We had been so close during our time in captivity.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you know whether they succumbed to the beatings while at the Srebrenica prison, or did this occur after an exchange?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Srebrenica prison. They never reached the hospital, or at least that's what Rado told me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Ms. Radovic, I thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Sellers. Now, Madam Radovic, you're going to be cross-examined by Madam Vidovic. You both speak the same language, and it's important that, because of that, that in order not to make it difficult for the interpreters to be able to give us a good interpretation, to allow an interval, a short interval of time between question and answer. Unfortunately, it happens when two of us are speaking the same language, be it English or be it Serbo-Croat. So please do allow a short interval. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Ms. Radovic.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is your testimony that you were a civilian and that you were distributing food to the Serbs who remained in Novo Selo to defend the Serb houses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I worked when I came. Over the weekend, I did distribute food to civilians. That is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In actual fact, those people were not civilians, were they?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you think they were? They were wearing civilian clothes. What else do you think they could have been?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, can you please just simply answer my questions. This is no place for us to argue. If you could just confine yourself to answering my questions, please. They were a well-organised Territorial Defence unit, they were part of the Zvornik TO, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How could they have been well organised? There weren't sufficient men there to begin with. Wearing civilian clothes, how can anyone call that an army? Please, just tell me one thing: This is a civilian court, I have no reason to hold back. Have you ever seen a soldier wearing civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because I think -- I notice that the atmosphere has suddenly changed in this courtroom. Madam Radovic, please try to remember what I told you yesterday when you were about to start giving your evidence: That once you have taken your place there on that chair, right in front of us here, you are no longer a witness of the Prosecution but you are a witness of this Tribunal. And I told you also that it is important that, in the course of your testimony, you treat the questions from the Prosecution and the questions from the Defence the same. I encouraged you to do your best not to discriminate between Prosecution and Defence. Madam Sellers is doing her duty here, and Madam Vidovic is doing her duty too. She has a right to ask you questions, and you have a duty to answer them. Unfortunately, I see that you have already picked up on each other, and that rather than answering the questions, that you are contesting Madam Vidovic and the way she is asking you questions. She has a right to put any question that she likes, and you have a duty to answer that question and not to argue with the lawyer. If the question that is put to you is not procedurally acceptable, the three of us will immediately ask you not to answer that question. But if we do not intervene, your duty is to answer that question. And please refrain from arguing with the lawyers, who are here doing their duty. Did I make myself clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I thank you for your cooperation. Yes, Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: May I make an additional remark in order to soften the situation? I don't know whether it's a question of translation, at least in the English version, it appears that the Defence counsel is contending that certain things had happened, for instance, whether the actual fact was those people were not civilians, that's the contention, and so far I think we do not have evidence for this, so I would suggest that you put your questions as questions and not as contentions. That way it will make it easier for the witness to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you, Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Zvornik TO unit, from the very beginning of the war, was, in fact, a well-equipped unit that had all sorts of equipment at their disposal, including tanks; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You weren't telling the truth, were you, when you said that the soldiers at Novo Selo and Drinjaca had no weapons or uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drinjaca is not close to where I live. I never spoke about Drinjaca, I was just speaking about Novo Selo. And the answer to your question is no.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, your testimony would be that the soldiers at Novo Selo had no weapons or uniforms.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did have weapons but not uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's true, in fact, isn't it, Mrs. Radovic, that they were a well-armed unit, with uniforms, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not have uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can I have the usher's assistance, please. Madam Usher, could you please place on the ELMO an excerpt from a document. This is an excerpt from a Zvornik Brigade document, "Salaries for June 1992, 2nd Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade." The title page of the excerpt bears the following number 1776899. Can the witness please look at page 01776956. 01776956. The heading is "List for the Drinjaca Lijesanj Mortar Platoon."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the names of these 11 people. Do you know any of these persons?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My dear, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you turn the page now to 01776991, the 2nd Battalion armoured units. If you can please look at the names of these persons here. Do you know any of these?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sweetheart.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, you were captured in the Drinjaca area.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Novo Selo, Drinjaca, the distance is 6 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's right. Do you not agree that if we look at this list, the Drinjaca area had a whole mortar platoon, even an armoured unit?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sweetheart, I can agree with the case you're putting to me, but I don't know any of these people. Drinjaca is 6 kilometres from where I live.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, one moment, one moment. I don't know whether it's a question of interpretation or not, but in answering the last three questions, in answering the last three questions, at least the interpretation tells us that not only has the atmosphere cleared up but that now the witness is referring or addressing Madam Vidovic as "sweetheart." Is it acceptable in your own language, or is it something that you object to? Because in my language, in these circumstances, that means -- that has a very ironic and cynical connotation. So I will stop it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it definitely does have ironic overtones, but what am I supposed to do about it? I can't say I mind particularly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The first time, I thought maybe it's a problem of interpretation, or that I was not really giving -- but then it was repeated. Madam Radovic, and this will be the last time I will say this --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours, I'm sorry to intervene, and I certainly don't think it's a precursor for Valentine's Day, but I would suggest that we might want to take a break at this point and then resume under calm conditions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. But before we take the break, I must make it clear that Madam Radovic, when you answer the questions, you are put a question -- you have a question forthcoming from Madam Vidovic, but then you address us, not Madam Vidovic. When you answer the question, you don't address the lawyer directly, you address us. And when you address us, you don't need to address us at all by any adjective or by any noun, just answer the question. If you choose at any moment to address Madam Vidovic, please address her as counsel or Madam Vidovic, but not as sweetheart. We'll have a 25-minute break. Just one moment. Madam Usher, could you escort the witness out, please, first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, could you bring the witness in, usher, please. Madam Vidovic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- you made use, before the break, of this document, the first page of which has ERN 01776899. Do you wish to tender that document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. That will be Defence Exhibit D189. Thank you. Now, let's proceed, and I hope that I had made myself clear enough before the break, and that I will not have the need to intervene again as we go along. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, is it true that all of the logistics, including weapons, equipment, and food, came to the units in Novo Selo and Drinjaca from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drinjaca, yes, but I don't know about Serbia, because that was far away.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You remember you gave a statement to the OTP in 2000.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On page 3 of that statement, page 3, paragraph 3 in the English, you said: "Food came from Serbia to Drinjaca on boats," and then from Drinjaca food was transported by car to Novo Selo.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mrs. Radovic, you were a soldier too, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were the chief cook in your unit, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Back in 2000, you told the OTP that you had given a statement to the Skelani police on the 7th or 8th of February, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was released from captivity, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have Madam Usher's assistance now, please. I would like to show the witness the official note on the statement. The date is the 7th of February, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, can you look at paragraph 2 of this note. I will quote. You said: "Muslims captured me on the 17th of September, 1992, in Novo Selo, near Drinjaca. I worked as the chief cook for soldiers of the Zvornik Territorial Defence." Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the usher now please again show the witness the document that we looked at a while ago, salaries for June 1992, 2nd Battalion. Prior to that, Your Honours -- actually, this document is D189, Defence Exhibit D189.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. In the meantime, do you want to tender this last document, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. May I suggest to you that, because of some other information that it contains, that it be tendered and kept under seal? Is there any objection on your part?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's no objection. Just a point of clarification, are we referring to the Zvornik statement or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, to the Zvornik statement. All right. You have no objection to that?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, Your Honour. I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document is being tendered and received as Defence Exhibit D190, and will be kept under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, can you please look again at this document, payment of salaries for June 1992, 2nd Battalion. Can you look at page 101776954, 2nd Battalion, Drinjaca Company, additional list. If you can look at the name under number 7, "Andja Radovic, cook." Is that your name here?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says. But I explained I'd never been mobilised. But if you want to have it that way, yes, it's my name.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, it is still your submission that you were a civilian and that you were cooking for civilians in Novo Selo.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, it is true, in fact, that not only were you not a civilian, but you were even captured wearing a uniform with a camouflage shirt. That is correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were aware of the situation of the Territorial Defence in the area of Drinjaca and Novo Selo.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in relation to Drinjaca. That's 6 kilometres from where I was, and Zvornik is 8 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were familiar with the general situation of the Territorial Defence in Novo Selo, were you not?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, I will now show you a map.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have the map placed on the ELMO. It's the Military Geography Institute. The map is for the Zvornik area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As we will be mentioning the names of certain places, would you please take a look at the map and tell the Trial Chamber, show them in fact, certain places so that we can orient ourselves. In order to make your task easier, I marked these places in yellow. There's a pointer in front of you, so please point to Zvornik, Cerska. Can you see Zvornik, Mrs. Radovic?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now Cerska, please.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Now please show Novo Selo to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Drinjaca.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Drinjaca is below that, Mrs. Radovic. Further below.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: There, thank you. Please show us Divic.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Show us Sapotnik, please.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Further below, Mrs. Radovic.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Kostjerovo?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Dzevanje?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Gornje Snagovo.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Liplje.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And please show us the village which Muslims call Pahljevici and Serbs called Paljevici. That's where it is.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Radovic. Perhaps you could now put your initials at the corner of the map, just as we did with the previous witness, because we would like this map to be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, we have no objection, but of course, just stating for the record, that the witness has merely identified things that have been premarked by the Defence on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we went through this before, Ms. Sellers. I don't know whether it was -- whether you were present or not at the time, but I thought it best to let it go rather than waste or lose time. Yes, this will be Defence Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- yes. This will be Defence Exhibit D191.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, I will put certain questions to you related to these villages. You've lived for a long time in that area, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Novo Selo. However, before the war, I didn't live there between January and September.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You lived in the Zvornik area for quite a while, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Petkovci.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Mrs. Radovic, it's true, isn't it, that before the war, Drinjaca had an ethnically mixed composition. There were a lot of Muslims living there.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you that I had nothing to do with Drinjaca, which is 6 kilometres away from where I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you told us yourself that 150 Muslims lived in Novo Selo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that the local Muslim population of Drinjaca, Novo Selo, and some other villages, in the course of May and April of 1992 -- in April, the Muslim residents of Novo Selo were expelled, their property looted, and houses burned out; is that true?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Many of your neighbours, Muslims, were killed, imprisoned in camps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The same happened to the Muslim population of Sopotnik, Kostjerovo, Liplje, Dzevanje, Gornje Snagovo, and other Muslim villages in the vicinity.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I only know about Novo Selo.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Liplje is quite close to the area where you lived?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Liplje is close to Divic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you want to say, or would you please say how far is that from the place where you lived?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: There, in April and May of 1992, was a camp in which there were 500 people imprisoned, many of whom were later killed. Have you ever heard of that?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, you moved about in that area. All of these things were happening to the Muslims, residents of Zvornik, and of the Zvornik area. Are you claiming that you don't know that, you're not aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the roads were blocked, and there was no way for me to know what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I didn't realise that you've already given a number to the exhibit. Now, would the technical booth be so kind as to show us a video. This is the video we showed during our opening statement. This is footage recorded by Mr. Martin Bell, a BBC journalist, in April 1992. Your Honours, we need just a few more minutes. It seems that we are having problems with the audio side of this tape.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can see the footage on our monitor, but I don't think that the rest of you can see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, let's go through it again. We saw -- I saw something, but it came and it went, so I don't know what the position is. And I could hear, of course, the audio. Let's try it again. I am on computer evidence, that's what I am using. No, at the moment, we certainly don't have anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, it's ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, while we're waiting for the technical problems to be solved, is this a video that's being tendered into evidence. I know we've seen several clips during the opening statement, and another clip that was shown with another witness. Is this one that's proposed to be submitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it will be.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think, Madam Vidovic, if it is at all possible for you to proceed with some other question for the time being until a technician comes over and solves this problem for us, I would appreciate that. If you prefer to wait, not to disrupt the sequence of your questioning, then obviously we will have a short break until this technical problem is fixed. It's up to you. I mean, it doesn't create any problems for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have a number of questions related to this video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So we will have a short break. Let's see whether it is at all possible to redress -- to fix this problem now, without the need for us to leave the courtroom. One moment. Let's give it another try. It says "playing" now. I had the same problem at home yesterday evening, and I couldn't fix it, so maybe I will learn something now. Yes, in the meantime, Judge Eser would like to put a question. To who?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: To the Defence. Just to ask the -- on this map, do we have the place of birth of the witness on this map? What is it called, Petkovci?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. That's to the north -- no, no, no, no, Your Honours, it's outside of this map. It is not shown on this map. It is to the north of Zvornik. I can see it on another map but not on the one that was tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: And how many kilometres distance from Zvornik? Perhaps you could ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, your village, can you tell us, how far is it from Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Twelve kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps I could turn to the questions pertaining to the arrest, and then we will come back to this issue, although it's not very logical. I think it's a better option than wasting time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, no, logic should not be sacrificed at all, and I see that you have a preference that this be fixed first before you proceed. So let's see if it can be fixed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, the Prosecution has no picture. I don't know if anyone else has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, we just have a black screen, the window of the software. And now we have moved to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, I don't quite know whether, in the course of the playing of this video, you will be relying on the visual as well as on the commentary. If you are running on the commentary, do you have a -- do you happen to have a transcript of it? I mean, I know that it is in English, but is there a transcript?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, Your Honour, we don't have the transcript, because this was a report by Martin Bell, in English. The words spoken in Bosnian are translated in subtitles, and I would like you to hear the words uttered by Mr. Bell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. Where do we stand? Perhaps the technician can give us an indication whether we ought to remain here or whether we ought to leave the courtroom, have a short break? It's up to you. Do you think you can solve it within the next couple of minutes? THE TECHNICIAN: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You need more than 10 minutes. Let's have a break of a few minutes. Let's do it this way: Registrar, please contact us in our chambers as soon as it is time to come back, okay? Thank you. Madam Radovic first. Yes, please. Sorry about this, Madam Radovic, but we have a technical problem, and there's no use sitting here looking at one another in this courtroom until it is solved, if it is solved. --- Break taken at 11.25 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, I'm sorry for all this. It was nobody's fault. It was a technical problem that we had. It seems with the laptop or notebook that you were using, Mr. Roberts, I understand that has been fixed to your satisfaction, because it's important that you do have a notebook that is in full functioning condition, all right? If you have any problems, do let us know. In the meantime, I kept the technician outside just in case we encounter further problems. Yes, shall we start with the playing of this video-recording? I want to know one thing: While the video is being played and it running commentary in English, as I explained before, will the interpreters be translating into B/C/S for the benefit of the witness, or is there a transcript in B/C/S of this video-recording?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as Mr. Martin Bell and other people are speaking in English, there will be a subtitle running in the Bosnian language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But I have followed some of this subtitling in the various videos we have seen, and most of the time, they are not a complete subtitling of what is being said. I mean, it's -- a lot is skipped. I can follow the language, although not completely, but I can also see that most of what is being said is missing. So what I suggest, if it does not create big problems to the B/C/S -- to the translation -- interpretation booths, do you think you'll be in a position to interpret the running commentary from English into B/C/S? Because the witness is going to be asked questions. I need a feedback from the B/C/S booth or the English booth.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Feedback is on its way, Your Honours. We're just switching channels. This is the B/C/S booth, Your Honour. The commentary in English is quite fast. Without a transcript, we are afraid that the booth will not be able to cover everything in any case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you don't have a transcript into English -- in English of this running commentary, do you?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What we can do is produce a transcript at a later stage. As for my questions to the witness, they will be of a general nature, so that I think she will be in a position to answer all my questions. But we shall see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's do it in a somewhat personalised manner. If there are any sectors of this video that you would like to base your questions upon, and I mean mostly the running commentary and not the visual, because the visual, you see it once, and you've seen it, but the running commentary, if it is not completely translated at the time may create problems. So in that case, could you please ask the technicians to stop the playing of the video, to rewind and then play back the section you want to concentrate your question or questions upon so that the interpreters will have then sufficient time to catch up with what they might have missed earlier on, all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So, Madam Radovic, you are going to watch a video-recording which goes back to April of 1992. This is a BBC video. And I would kindly ask you to pay absolute attention to what you see and what you hear, because then you are going to be asked questions by Madam Vidovic based on what you see and what you hear. If you have any problems with following this video, both the visual and the audio part, please draw our attention straightaway and we'll try to rectify it, all right? Did you understand me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's start with the video-recording. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, during your testimony yesterday, you mentioned that at some point in April 1992, you were not able to go to work. You mentioned a place called Karakaj. What you have now seen in this video, was that the reason you were not free to move about?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
