utterances.text: This wasn't something that I could see. It was too far away. We couldn't even go as far as the first tunnel, let alone any further.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, it's true, isn't it, that what you saw in this video is something that happened precisely in the villages that you indicated on the map. Some of those villages were only a kilometre from your own village. Is it possible that you saw none of this?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the fact that the entire Muslim population of the area was expelled in April and May 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not Novo Selo. I don't know about the rest.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's true, in fact, isn't it, that 150 Muslims of Novo Selo were driven out. Some managed to return to the area in early June. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if some escaped. I didn't know that many of them. I know there were quite a number of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The local Serb population of Drinjaca and Novo Selo, which is where you lived, units from Dzevanje and Kamenica, that is the list, or rather, that is the unit that we showed you a while ago. Your name is on that list. They were involved in the ethnic cleansing of the Muslim population, were they not?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As early as June 1992, the local Serb population, including Serbs from Novo Selo, was part of the 2nd Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the civilians. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance, please. I would like to show the witness a document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's unclear to me at this time. Are we finished with the video questions, are we tendering that, or are we moving on to a subsequent document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, you can answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the questions to follow will be related to what was shown on the video, and I will certainly make it clear that I wish to tender the video. My question was whether these units were involved in ethnic cleansing. That was my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, please look at this document. It's a document by the Zvornik garrison command. The date is 3rd of August, 1992. The number is 017766815. Salaries -- recapitulation of paid salaries to members of units of the Zvornik infantry brigade for June 1992. Can you please look at this document. Look at the list under the unit name, and you will see there brigade command, headquarters: 1st Battalion, 2nd Battalion, 3rd Battalion, liaison platoon, military police, engineers, tank detachment, Divic, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I know nothing of Divic and Drinjaca. As for the 2nd Battalion, they used to come over to Drinjaca and probably to Novo Selo. The 3rd Battalion, I know nothing about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You do agree, don't you that it would have taken a great many soldiers to expel the Muslim population of the entire area.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree, but we were the first to be expelled.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that the Serbs were the first to be expelled, and only then the Muslims? Is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, of course. On the 17th, we all left and they stayed. And I know nothing about what happened after the 17th of September.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like now, at this point in time, to tender the video into evidence and be assigned an exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would just like to state that what was said in the video, be it in English or B/C/S, was only for the purpose that it was said and not necessarily for the truth of it, stated for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Obviously. I take it for granted that by now, having started this trial in October, you're both familiar with the fact that we are three professional Judges here, and by no means we are looking at what Mr. Bell states or what is said in the commentary as evidence of what was happening at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. I just make it for the record's sake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, it's obvious. So you can put your mind at rest, because most of you will be making use of this kind of evidence, all right? So the position is made very clear. I think I made it clear from the very outset that it's like that. Yes, in the meantime, I think --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may explain, in order to avoid further confusion and objections of this kind, videos and other types of evidence is something I show witnesses to comment on. As for our Defence case, we're not going to be proving something we think needs proving. Your Honour, I'm not sure if we have been assigned a number or Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, not yet. This will be Defence Exhibit D192. We're talking, just for the record, we're talking of the document which, in the B/C/S version, has ERN 01776815 -- 6815, and consists of two pages, the second of which is the English translation of the same. The video, I think, has already been tendered. No?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, Your Honour. That is precisely why we have requested a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you are tendering this video. Can I have the technical indications of it? It is Michael Bell?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Martin Bell, BBC.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Martin Bell, April 1992, in Zvornik. So the video-recording which was played earlier, namely, the BBC -- having the title "BBC, Martin Bell, April 1992 - Zvornik" is being tendered in evidence by the Defence and is being admitted and marked as Defence Exhibit D193. D193. Do you have any objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, no, we don't have any objections. We would just request a copy of the video from the Defence to make our files complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure that will be done, Madam Vidovic. I thought this had been done because this was shown.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By all means, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, you and your husband were members of the 2nd Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade from June 1992 onwards, were you not?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My husband was. As for myself, I'm not sure how many times I have to repeat this: I was put on some sort of list, that's true, but I don't know who did it on my behalf. My husband did have a rifle but not a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Radovic. The 2nd Battalion was a large unit, was it not? It had about 1.200 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Twenty-three in Novo Selo, 23 men and seven women, would you call that a large unit? I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your husband, Stanoje Obradovic, was, in actual fact, a member of the Kamenica unit.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was in Novo Selo. He never budged from me. Whenever I came home, I would always find him there, our house or our brother-in-law's house, which is 800 metres from our house.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the usher's assistance now, please, to place on the ELMO an extract from the Zvornik Brigade document, 01776899, which is salaries for June 1992, 2nd Battalion. If the witness can please be shown the page 01776964. If you could look at the section where the name of the unit of the 2nd Battalion is stated, the Dzevanje Kamenica Company.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then if you could turn the page, please, 01776968, and look at number 85.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stanoje?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that your husband's name?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now please look at the last page of this document, and the number is 01776970. If you could look at the figures in relation to members of this unit, it's 126, isn't it, 126. This unit was a large unit for a small village like that, was it not?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I have no idea who Sreten Micic is, for example, Milos Dragutinovic, Dragan Micic, Milan Micic, Milenko Ristanovic, Ivan Lukic, Milos Mirkovic, Ivan Mirkovic, Miso Mirkovic, Mitar Stojanovic, Zivoin Ivanovic, Marjan Zecevic, I know this one. Dusan Milicevic, I don't know these people. I can't say anything against them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, I don't expect you to speak against these people. My question is as follows: Please, it is true that the units of which your husband was a member had a lot of people from outside, more people from outside than locals; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I wasn't there all the time. I only know the people from my village, but I don't know any of the others. Probably, when the attack took place, they came over. I can't say they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this exhibit now be assigned a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course, Madam Vidovic. This is being tendered and admitted as --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think it's the same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Look at it, Madam Vidovic. The first page of D189 is, indeed, 01776899, like this one. The second page is 6954. What's happening, registrar, is the first page is the same, because it shows the title of the document itself, but the rest isn't, so it has to be given a different number. So this document is being tendered by the Defence. There is no objection, I take it, Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's no objection to the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, there is no objection forthcoming from the Prosecution, and it is being admitted and marked as Defence Exhibit D193 -- 4? 194, D194. Oh, yes, D193 was the video. Let's proceed. We can finish this witness -- yes, Judge Eser would like to put a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Before we leave this exhibit, witness, would you draw your attention to number, what was it, number 85 on the ELMO. Do we still have it on the ELMO? The last exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: You told us that this is the name of your husband.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: On the same line, you'll see a signature. Can you recognise this signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Line 85, we have the name of your husband, and at the end of this line there is a signature. Now, do you recognise this signature? Do you know who may have signed this? Is it the signature of your husband?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: It's just interesting that there are signatures, the same type, quite a few of them above them, and after -- starting with 88, there have been signatures also by the same person. Thank you. So you would not recognise this signature as that of your husband?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may, since this is a situation that is likely to happen again, I asked for information on these documents. If a military unit was on the ground, then someone else would have been entitled to receive their salaries and then forward them to the persons that the salaries belonged to. That was the explanation we got, but we shall be calling on witnesses in our case that will be in a position to provide more accurate explanations on documents such as these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the time being, I do agree with Madam Vidovic that we have had one witness who gave an indication that there were instances where there was someone with a power of attorney who was drawing salaries on behalf of -- but as to the rest, we don't have evidence. So what you have stated in regard to this submission cannot be taken, in any way, as evidence, Madam Vidovic. Yes, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, even before the war, and especially after the war broke out, local Serb residents underwent intensive military training in the centre in Divic, including your husband.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My husband, in Divic? No. The two of us went to work together, and would come back before the roads became blocked.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you claiming that the local Serb residents were not trained in the training centre in Divic, which is located near your village?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't think that was the case. How could they have organised training in Divic? I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please put an excerpt from a document of the Zvornik Brigade on the ELMO. The ERN number is 01776862, "Payment of Salaries for June 1992, Brigade Staff and Divic Training Centre."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have an extra copy here, register.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to take a look, Mrs. Radovic? Please take a look at the document. It says there that in June, there were 14 people at this training centre. Have you ever heard of this fact?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know any of the people on this list.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, one moment. The question also included whether you knew of the existence of this training centre in Divic. Did you ever hear or come to know of a training centre in Divic? I take it that Divic is a place, no, a place name.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question was twofold. Let me put the two questions to you separately. Madam Radovic, did you ever hear about a training centre in Divic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So the second question: Look at the list of the persons that you find on the second page of the document that you have been handed. Do you know any of those persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know any of them, Jokic Dragan, or any others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not even Miladin Obradovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I don't think it's the case of putting the third question, because obviously she won't be in a position to answer it. So do you want to tender this into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This will be D195; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, it is your testimony that soldiers of the 2nd Battalion, for whom you cooked, or people from the 2nd Battalion, for whom you cooked, sat peacefully in their homes in June of 1992 and onwards; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had to protect their homes, in civilian clothes. How shall I put it to you? They did not have uniforms. They were there, protecting their homes. I was away from my home, so what was there for me to protect?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The truth is, Mrs. Radovic, that, starting in June 1992 and onwards, the people from Novo Selo terrorised the Muslim residents of the village of Pahljevici who attempted to continue living in their homes, as well as part of Novo Selo and the village of Bajrici to which the Muslims returned in 1992. You lived there.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where Pahljevici is. I don't know whether that's in the direction of Drinjaca or Zvornik. I really don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Serbs from Novo Selo and Drinjaca started something called St. Vitus's offensive against the Muslims, and that this offensive was started in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just told you that I knew nothing about what was going on in Drinjaca. That was 6 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, I asked you about Novo Selo as well. A large number of Serb troops were stationed in Novo Selo, in June of 1992, and from there they launched an offensive against Muslim villages; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't leave in June. I don't know, I simply don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mrs. Radovic. Now I will turn to something else, namely, your arrest. The people who arrested you wore black uniforms; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement you gave to the Prosecutor in 2000, you stated, and you confirmed it yesterday, that the men in black uniforms were called Zenges and belonged to special forces. That's what you said.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said, and that's what I heard when I got to this place. Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: ZNG, actually, are units of the Croatian army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never inquired about that. I was very fearful, so I never asked anyone about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: However, it is a well-known fact in our region, isn't it, Mrs. Radovic?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, a well-known fact?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That members of ZNG are actually members of the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I didn't ask anyone. It's just that when my neighbour asked me, Do you know who had hit you, I said that I didn't know, and then he explained to me that the man who hit me was Zenge or a member of ZNG.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When speaking of Muslims in the village, you said they wore camouflage uniforms and that all their people were in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Local Muslims never wore black uniforms; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you were arrested, you were beaten by Zenges, members of the ZNG; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, local Muslims saved you and helped you in that situation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Kadrija helped me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the Muslim hamlet, they treated your wounds.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Refik, who was the nurse.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Moreover, the Muslim family Sahbaz and his wife gave you Muslim clothes and tried to hide you in their home.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I apologise, I forgot to mention this: I was given pantaloons when I was in the shelter. As for Sahbaz and his wife, they helped me and they took me into their house on the 4th of October. That's when they helped me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that they wanted to humiliate you by giving you Muslim clothes to wear and assigning a Muslim name to you, or do you think it was done for some other reasons?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was done to humiliate me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, I have been following and trying to hope for an improvement, but you are not allowing for an interval between question and answer, and I am actually really surprised that the interpreters are succeeding in catching up with what is going -- with what is being said. It's being made very difficult for them. So if you could please slow down, both of you, and allow a short interval, I'm sure that you will make everyone's life a little easier. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, they actually took off the uniform that you wore at the time so that somebody didn't -- so that people wouldn't kill you because of the uniform.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not right. Anybody can confirm that I wore a skirt and a shirt, and also some shoes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because I need the cooperation of everyone here. It just occurs to my mind, as we approach 12.30, which is usually the time for the next break, that we have had stoppages during this session, so I don't quite know whether it's the case of having the break as scheduled at 12:30 and then we'll resume, of course, after 25 minutes, or whether it's the case of proceeding. I don't know, I mean it's -- because it involves technicians, interpreters, and I see that the sitting is proving to be a little bit heavy. Okay. Madam Vidovic, just for your direction, for your information, we will be stopping in about two, three minutes' time, so you choose the time when -- or we will be stopping because we need to. Then we will have a shorter break, we will have a 20-minute break rather than a 25-minute break, and try to catch up. Do you think you will be able to finish with this witness today or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so. I think I will be able to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So shall we have the break now, or do you want to go on -- proceed with a couple of other questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps a couple more questions, very brief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, we just mentioned the Muslim family, Sahbaz and his wife. It is true, isn't it, that you spent at least seven days with them, as long as it was safe for you to remain there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mehmed Juzunovic, a local Muslim resident, gave you his wife's sweater, whereas his wife Ajka brought food to you in the shelter where you were, milk and sugar; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: While in shelter, there was an attempt to attack you which was prevented by Mehmed, a local Muslim; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I mentioned Omer, local Muslim. That was his name; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that time he said, If something happens to her, I will kill five of your men; is that right, that those were the words he directed to the members of the ZNG?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that while you were in the shelter, that two people tried to attack you. One of them was a woman with a foreign accent, known as Hosovka.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Those were also the people who were not local Muslims.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I believe that they were not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is true, isn't it, that the local Muslims saved you on that occasion as well?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we can have our break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. We will have a 20-minute break, starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, when you came to the prison in Cerska, which is what you called the stable, you found Branko Sekulic there, as well as Jakov Dzokic, Dragan Ilic, and Rado Pejic, called Miso; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you saw them around the 5th of October, they were already in fairly bad shape; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On page 8 of your statement given to the investigators of this Tribunal, on the last page of the Bosnian version, which is page 9, you described them in the following way: "They were all pale, covered in bruises. They had been beaten severely. All of them said that, prior to my arrival, a lot of soldiers beat them every day."

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were pale, but they did not have bruises at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, did you state something like this to the investigators?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear what the witness answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Madam Radovic, the interpreters couldn't hear your answer. What was the answer? The question was: "Mrs. Radovic, did you state something like this to the investigators?" And you said -- I heard you say -- I heard you say something, but it's the interpreters who need to translate it to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were pale. They were not bruised. They were pale and exhausted when I arrived at the stable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the question remains: Did you, at any time, tell the investigators that, prior to your arrival, a lot of soldiers had beaten them every day? Did you ever say these words to the investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They told me that that was so, most likely, but I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, okay, thank you. Madam Vidovic, let's move.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your 2000 statement, you also said that Branko Sekulic had been wounded and that his wound was infected, that there were maggots, and that that was the situation as you found it when you arrived.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that a certain Alaga, in your presence, beat Branko with fists, kicked him, and beat him with a wooden bat, so that his blood sprayed throughout the whole stable, that blood leaked from his mouth and nose.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And ears too.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Alaga beat even you.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You described in detail daily beatings of these four men in the stable. You even said that, due to these blows, Sekulic became deaf and was barely able to walk.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In that stable, it was generally very cold.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: There was no heating.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It was dirty.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The men had old coats on them, shoes with holes. They didn't have any socks on.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Savko Huric occasionally brought some socks to us. Otherwise, we didn't have any socks.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The men were in such bad shape that they couldn't even shave when the local Muslims brought them in soap and razors.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never received soap or razors.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, is it your testimony that you never mentioned anything of this nature to the investigators?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody ever asked me whether the men shaved. I didn't see them shaving while I was there. They didn't have any shavers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Sekulic was in such a poor shape that, on the way between Cerska and Srebrenica, he and some soldiers had to stay behind and spend the night in a stable.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he stayed behind with one soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, it is true, isn't it, that these men actually arrived in Srebrenica half dead from the beatings which frequently resulted in them fainting.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind what you told us about the conditions at the stable in Cerska, would you be surprised -- would you have been surprised if some of these men died shortly thereafter as a result of the conditions and injuries they had received while staying at the stable?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody died at the stable. All of us went to Srebrenica, Dragan, Jakov, Rado, and I. Branko stayed behind. After I was released, Jakov, Dragan, and Branko died.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will repeat my question. Mrs. Radovic, please listen carefully to my question. I asked you something else entirely. In view of what you have told us about the conditions prevailing in that stable, I asked you whether you would have been surprised had one of these men died shortly thereafter as a result of the conditions at the stable. I'm not claiming that they, in fact, died, I'm just saying whether you would have been surprised whether, due to injuries and difficult conditions there, they died.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had we stayed longer there, perhaps, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, you told us that you were slapped and beaten as well at the stable.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean Alaga?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Rado Pejic was also in the stable when you were slapped and beaten, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that other prisoners told you that you lost consciousness as a result of a blow that Alaga dealt you.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Rado Pejic was there.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What's more, you say that he was the one who told you that Alaga had hit you so hard that you, in fact, lost consciousness.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other three men told me. Branko was the only one who was unable to even speak.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The essence of my question was: You said that Rado Pejic told you that you had received such a hard blow; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said in your testimony yesterday that you were moved from the stable on the 26th of January, 1993. You were very specific about the date.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How do you know what the date was of your transfer to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I know about the 26th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What happened, in fact, is that you were shown documents to jog your memory, were you not?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Based on what is it, then, that you are sure about the date, that it was the 26th of January?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was that conscious. I still remember the date I was captured, the date I was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's okay. For a moment, I needed to check the transcript, to check whether I had heard well or not. But I did hear well. Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, did you keep track of the dates during your time in --

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in captivity?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't keep track on a daily basis. But we were aware of some of the dates, and we specifically remembered the 26th of January as the date we left the stable.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. The person who introduced himself as Zulfo Tursunovic and said that he would take you to the prison in Srebrenica in order to be exchanged, this person saw you in Cerska, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, this person did not come to the stable itself; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He took us outside of the stable.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement from the year 2000, page 13, paragraph 2 of the Bosnian version, in the English it's page 13, paragraph 5, you said, I quote: "Two soldiers wearing camouflage uniforms escorted us to the centre of Cerska. The men had been badly beaten, and we were all in a very poor condition. In the centre, we were met by three Muslim soldiers with camouflage uniforms, carrying three automatic rifles. One of these men said, 'I am Zulfo Tursunovic and I will take you to the prison in Srebrenica for exchange.' Zulfo had grey hair, and was about 190 centimetres tall." So what you told the investigators on that occasion is essentially that Zulfo took you over in Cerska. What is correct, then?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe Zulfo took us away and walked with us all the way to Srebrenica. I can't remember specifically.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said in relation to that person, Zulfo Tursunovic, that he had grey hair, or greying hair, rather. That's what you told the investigators, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you described him yesterday, you provided a very different description. You said that he had black hair, which is quite different.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said he was tall, I said he was burly. He carried an automatic rifle, a pistol, and a Motorola. And he was very fair to us. And I abide by what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not trying to challenge that, but you described the same person to the investigators as someone with greying hair, and yesterday you said black hair. Do you agree with me that these are two different things?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my dear lawyer, do you think that 12 years later, you yourself would be able to focus on all the details?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it possible, Mrs. Radovic, precisely for that reason, that you saw Zulfo for the first time in Cerska?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you had walked from Cerska to Srebrenica in one day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know - I assume you must know - that the distance is about 40 kilometres, across hillside, during war?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We walked through hills, but we didn't keep track of the exact distance. We spent the whole day travelling, and we came there late in the evening. It was nighttime; we couldn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that you walked all the way?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were all in a poor condition. It is your submission that you were able to actually walk the distance in a single day?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had no choice.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Rado Pejic, too, walked along with you, didn't he? The whole day.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you say that Branko Sekulic stayed behind and did not reach Srebrenica with you.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You arrived at the prison in Srebrenica on the 26th of January, 1993, you claim, and you stayed there for 12 days.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You watched what was going on around you, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I could see was what was in my room, but nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were in that room together with other women.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Including Milena Mitrovic.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember Milena Mitrovic, I remember the ones I've mentioned. She may have been there, but I just don't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said yesterday that there were two women called Milena in the room with you.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were two, but I don't know their last names. One was captured together with her daughter, and her daughter was injured.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. During your stay in Srebrenica, you were only interrogated once, were you not?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were interrogated by a rather young man. This was, in fact, the only person who ever interrogated you at the prison in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not inside the prison, it was behind the prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, my reference is to the period of time that you spent in prison, and my question is: Did I understand you correctly when you said that this man was wearing a blue uniform?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had a uniform. I can't remember the colour. He was fair and he was respectful, and he asked me a number of questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said he wore a blue uniform. Could this have been a police uniform from the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said today that you, too, were slapped by someone in the prison, in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A young man came in and slapped me twice, but I don't know who he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But, Mrs. Radovic, in your earlier statements, and again I'm referring to a statement you made to OTP investigators, you failed to mention, in fact, that anyone had hit you at all. What's more, you stated that you had not been beaten in the prison in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did say yesterday clearly that I was slapped twice, didn't I? No one can take this away from me, the beating that I suffered. I know all of the beating; I remember every single time I was slapped. Please forgive me if you found this insulting.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Essentially, my question is this: This is very difficult to bear, slaps and blows. I wonder why it was that you failed to mention anything about it to the investigators of this Tribunal when you were questioned by them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, if you look at the witness statement of the 24th, 25th, 27th of March, I'm referring to the English version, page 13, last paragraph, third, fourth, and fifth line: "One of the soldiers was wearing sunglasses, although it was dark in that room. He had a very short haircut. He slapped me and he beat the other three men." So she has made the distinction, and she has -- between slapping and beating, and she has also stated that she was slapped. So I don't think it's the case of you suggesting to her that she never mentioned to the investigator that she was slapped. Then, if you look at the second page -- the next page, page 14, you see the third paragraph before the end: "I was not beaten or sexual assaulted at the Srebrenica prison. I was slapped the first day, but not after that." So if anything, there is an affirmation that she was slapped once and not more than once, and that's the only thing that you can suggest to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may be allowed to clarify. The witness' statement in relation to the slapping was about the SUP building. When she spoke about what happened in the prison itself, where there were men too, she said as follows: "I was not beaten in the prison in Srebrenica or sexual assaulted." She was quite specific about that. As for what happened first, she spoke about this as about something that happened in the MUP building, so maybe that's what has caused this misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I don't believe the witness has ever mentioned the word "MUP" or "SUP", and I think she might be referring generically as her imprisonment as a prison. But we can clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I quite agree with you, Ms. Sellers, and at the end of the day, what difference is it going to make? Anyway, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, you did not see the male prisoners after you were separated from them; is that a fact?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement to the OTP, you never mentioned that you exchanged greetings with them, did you?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that we exchanged greetings on the 6th, when we left. I did say that, I'm positive.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I mean the statement you made to the investigators, Mrs. Radovic.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I clearly said that I'd asked Gedza, in the evening, he allowed me to shake hands and to exchange greetings.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Mrs. Radovic, it's true, isn't it, that there was a woman who was wounded in the room with you.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a girl.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: A girl, fair enough. She was given medical assistance, wasn't she?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the room. I'm not sure if they ever took her anywhere else, but no medical assistance came to our room. I don't want to speak about anything else. I only spent a very short time with them, and that's all I feel I can talk about.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it your testimony, then, that no doctors ever came to the prison at the time?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to our room, for as long as I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony, you mentioned Ilija Ivanovic. You do remember that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that he had been exchanged with you on the 6th of February, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You're absolutely positive that Ilija Ivanovic was exchanged with you on that day.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am absolutely positive. He had been captured near Ovaci. He Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. couldn't speak properly; he had epilepsy or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay, I'll ask you something else now. I'll just ask you another question about the conditions in the prison. You said that there was a stove there, but you didn't have any firewood, so there was no heating in the room; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: There was no heating at all, you mean?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the evening we heard we were going to be exchanged, Gedza came and ordered some firewood to be used and make a fire. But that was very rare.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you did say that one of the prisoners --

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said Ilija. I know what I said, I'm very clear about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that firewood had been brought to you, but you also say that there was no heating except once or twice. Now, which is true?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was very seldom that there was any heating. Ilija would be allowed to go outside and fetch firewood.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you a different thing now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown a document shown by the Prosecutor, P491. The number is 02075668. This document should be a document of the Srebrenica armed forces staff, 19/23, dated the 6th of February, 1993. If the witness could please have a look.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, I have several questions about this. After you left the prison, you spoke to many people from Republika Srpska about what had happened to you in captivity; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I talked to no one. The international court came to my mother-in-law's place, and they took me to the Drina Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you gave a statement to the Ministry of the Interior, to the security service, at Skelani?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did when I was first captured. I think I did, but I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When you were first captured or when you were first released? I don't know, it may be a question of translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I was released.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that you then gave them your personal information: Date of birth, place of birth, husband's name?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You described in detail how you were captured and who the persons were who came with you from Cerska to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned your husband too. This is something you've said before. Your husband had no official military assignment in Karakaj, did he?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. We had no access to Karakaj.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't say this to any of the people who interviewed you at any time, the Muslims who asked you questions or interrogated you in the prison.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said, and when asked you confirmed, that the young man who interrogated you was fair and respectful, and that the interrogation took a brief while only.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it --

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that you were not interrogated about the Serb military units or their commanders?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had my documents right there to see.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, my question is: Did the Muslims ask you questions about Serb units and their respective commanders?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. It was 12 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, can you now please focus on this: In your 2000 statement, you said that you had been interrogated a day after you had been brought to Srebrenica, which you confirmed today; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not correct. No one questioned me a day after I got to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, Mrs. Radovic, that you were questioned or interrogated one day after you arrived in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no one interrogated us. They only told us that we would be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, Mrs. Radovic, can you please look at this document in front of you. The heading is: "Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina Armed Forces, Staff Security Organ 19/23." The date is 6th of February, 1993. It's true, isn't it, that you did not give any statements on or about that date in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 19th, I gave no statements whatsoever to anyone. 19/23, 6th of February, I gave no statement at all. The 6th of February is when we left.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But something else is also true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the witness can please now be shown the statement -- actually, this is P190 -- or D190. D190. You can use my copy, if that's convenient.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at this, Mrs. Radovic. Please take a look at the first sentence. It's true, isn't it, that on that day, the 6th of February, 1993, you gave a statement to the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska, Public Security Station in Skelani. Please take a look at this. The first sentence says: "On the 6th of February, 1993, an interview was conducted with Andja Radovic." My question is as follows: Do you agree that, immediately upon your exchange, you talked to the Serbian police in Skelani?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most likely I did, although I don't remember that, because we went to a hotel there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Usher, I just want to make sure, because I was following the transcript and not the video, I want to make sure that you do not put that document on the ELMO. All right, okay. Thank you. Yes, my apologies to you, Madam Vidovic. Could you proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now please be shown document P19.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, would you please briefly take a look at this document. So it's document P19, first page. The title is "Persons Kept in Detention Locally and Measures Undertaken with Respect to Them." Mrs. Radovic, we have heard here that you knew Rado Pejic as well, and that you saw him alive upon leaving the prison; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at number 17. The name there, it says "Rado Pejic, son of Mihajlo." To the right is a notation, "died." The first date is not clear, but the second date says "03/92."

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rado is alive, Rado didn't die.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When answering the questions put by the Prosecutor today, you said that it was nighttime when you arrived. But prior to that, would you please take a look at another document, P15. P15, please. You told us that what you arrived in Srebrenica, it was nighttime; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, then, that it could not have been 1700 hours, or 5.45 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have my watch, so I didn't know what time it was. I just knew that it was dark.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want to bring the Trial Chamber's attention, she said she remembered the lights were on, that it was getting dark. And in her mind, it might have been approaching nighttime. I don't think it had any relationship to the exact time of day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I was about to put that question, and I ask that I be allowed to complete my questions. I don't see the point of an objection of this nature, because I wasn't finished with my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, at 1745 hours, it is usually not dark in our region, is it?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean it's not? It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you are telling us that in February, in our region, it is usually dark at that hour; is that what you're claiming?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You also told us that the lights were on.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you wish to say that, in Srebrenica, at that time when you arrived, there was electrical power?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no electricity, but the candles were lighted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I do have to interrupt again, and I give my apologies to Defence counsel. I believe that we're talking about January, when she arrived, and not February.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you are right. Knowing something about the subject, I think I have a very clear idea what time it gets dark in that region, also because I don't live far away from there, and I have sailed to the region so I know exactly what time difference there is and how it affects daytime and nighttime. You do have also -- that is something that I don't know, but do you apply summer time -- or in 1992 and 1993, did you apply summer time in your country, like the rest of Europe, or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not sure about that. However, it is the same season as it is now, and in Sarajevo, it is not dark at that hour. It is possible that the situation is somewhat different in that region, but it wasn't my intention to mislead the witness. If I said February, it is possible that I simply --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Forget that and let's proceed. Let's move, because we've got five minutes left for this session.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I will put just one more question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, today, or perhaps yesterday, you mentioned the fact that you talked to Rado Pejic at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you're sure that he told you that Jakov Dzokic had died.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jakov, Dragan, and Branko, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you're sure that he told you that Jakov Dzokic had died.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I've concluded my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know these people here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic, particularly for your cooperation in finishing well within the time limit we had. Is there a re-examination, Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'll try to make it as brief as possible. I would like for the witness to be given Defence Exhibit 190. Again, I believe this is the one that we do not want to put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This, you must not put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would just like to ask, Ms. Radovic, if you look toward the bottom of this statement given to the Public Security Station in Skelani, would you tell me whether you have signed the bottom of this statement or not? Do you see your signature?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not my signature. I can show you my signature. This here is not my signature. Do you want me to sign something now?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, thank you. Thank you very much for the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Also, I'd like to go to Defence Exhibit D189, and we will turn to the page number that ends in ERN 54.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I just say quickly, for the record, that for the last document, it doesn't purport to be a signature either, so there's no question of a forgery of her signature, just so that's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I agree with you, Mr. Jones, and I mean, I think the answer that the witness gave was the answer that Ms. Sellers was expecting, in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I just didn't want it to be thought that someone had tried to forge her signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, it's okay. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you look on line number 7. I believe that your name is written there, and would you follow that line along to the other side of the page and tell the Trial Chamber whether you signed this document concerning salaries.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Is that your signature there?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could I ask the usher possibly to assist, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, page 6994 --

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, this is not my signature. Do you want me to sign something now so that all of you can see what my signature looks like? I really want to be of assistance to you so that you can see what my signature looks like.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, I believe that's fine. I just wanted to see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We already have your signature, Madam Radovic, because you signed two statements which you gave to the Prosecution, so we don't need your signature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you can compare the handwriting. If it is necessary, Your Honour, I can sign both in Cyrillic and Latinic script.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not necessary. I think it shows that you don't have expertise of what these proceedings are. Ms. Sellers is precisely expecting you to say no, that is not my signature. That's why she put the question. Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would also like to ask you, concerning the uniformed people that are referred to as the Zenge, were they assisting the people in camouflage uniforms that you've described as Muslim soldiers when you were arrested and then subsequently imprisoned? Was that your impression, that they were assisting them?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And was it also your impression that even the Muslims, who were very kind and treated you with considerable respect while you were in Novo Selo and then in Cerska, related to you that they were unable to release you or to no longer make you an imprisoned person?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't dare.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And were you imprisoned by people in camouflage uniform who were Bosnian Muslim soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And then my last question, I would just like to go back to Exhibit P15. On this exhibit, I would like to draw your attention to what is the bottom of the first page that I have in the English, and where it states that "it is improbable that she knows any reliable information about the Chetniks that could be of significance. She only knows of," and then the name of one person, "allegedly a commander from the Chetnik units." Was this, or does this appear to be the conclusion that the questioner, interrogator, reached after speaking to you in the Srebrenica prison?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think it is fair to ask this question to the witness, because how can she answer -- confirm or not confirm, whether this was the conclusion. It was the conclusion. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'll withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She didn't draw up this document, she's not the author of the document, and she doesn't even remember who the person was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: One last question, and that concerns the prisoner Ilija Ivanovic. Would you describe that person as having been handicapped or crippled, the person who was exchanged with you?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't know that he was epileptic, but when we started out, he wasn't stable on his feet. And when we were on the truck, he almost fell on me, and I pushed him away. And then I was afraid that I had injured him. And then a woman helped me -- helped him, and he regained his composure.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions. I do want to make one comment about a Prosecution exhibit, and it's P19, to inform Your Honours that the date that is on this exhibit in the English says 3 February 1993. We are asking for a revised translation. After having spoken to the translators, it's uncertain as to whether that's 23 February or 3 February. And I would like to advise you that we will be submitting another translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you. No questions? Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Mrs. Radovic, I would like to bring you back to the meetings with Zulfo Tursunovic. You met him at least on two occasions, one in Cerska when you have been exchanged -- when he came and he told you that you would be exchanged, and then you would say -- the question is: Was it -- did you have the impression that he said so, that it was his own decision that you should be exchanged, or did you have the impression that he was somehow advised by somebody else? You mentioned that he was acting on somebody else's instructions - that was what I have in English - on somebody else's instructions. What to you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Could Your Honour just refer us to that part because I don't remember that part of her testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I have it here on somebody else's instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I also wonder whether she could really assist with whether Zulfo Tursunovic was acting on his own or on any orders. I don't know if it's something she can help with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She did mention something for sure along those lines. But anyway, we can direct the witness to answer the question. Should I read the question out to you again, Madam Radovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Eser asked you the following question, he told you: "I would like to bring you back to the meetings with Zulfo Tursunovic. You met him at least on two occasions, one in Cerska when you have been exchanged -- when he came and told you that you would be exchanged, and then you would say -- the question is: Was it -- did you have the impression that he said so, that it was his own decision that you would be exchanged, or did you have the impression that he was somehow advised by somebody else to tell you that you would be exchanged." Do you recall whether he had told that -- that he was telling you that you would be exchanged because someone else had advised him that this would be the case?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He simply told us that he had to bring us alive to Srebrenica. He didn't tell us whether it was on somebody's orders. We had to cover all that distance on foot. It's hard to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Now, on the second occasion, when you have been in Srebrenica, you told us that Zulfo Tursunovic left the room for a moment, when you have -- or some of you have been beaten, and when he returned, that he was angry against the other people. And did you have the impression that he had some sort of authority with regard to the people, to the persons, who maltreated you in this room?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA RADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I take it that there are no further questions, which means that your testimony comes to an end here. I will just say a few words. First of all, I would like to thank you, Madam Radovic, on behalf of Judge Brydensholt and Judge Eser and also on behalf of the Tribunal, for having come over to give testimony in this case. I know that testifying on these events is never easy, particularly for someone like you. And I want to assure you that, as soon as you leave this courtroom, you will receive all the attention and all the assistance you require to enable you to return home without any undue delay. I also wish to wish you a safe journey back home, on behalf of everyone here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to greet everybody here, wish you success and happiness in your further work, and I'm very glad that I was able to spend this time here with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, I thank you, madam. You may now withdraw. Before we rise, I should like to express the Chamber's gratitude to all the officers of this courtroom, not only those present inside the courtroom but, of course, the technicians, the interpreters. We have exceeded our time limit by about eight minutes. I did not seek your permission before we did so, so I apologise for that, and I thank you for having cooperated so that we could finish with this witness and send her back home as early as possible, and without keeping her here unnecessarily for another day. I thank you. We will reconvene tomorrow. We'll have the new witness. Please try to make an effort to finish with the new witness tomorrow. The reason is that you know that on Friday, we have a Plenary and I, for sure, will not be able to -- we won't be sitting while we are having a Plenary. So, if possible, we'll try to finish with the witness tomorrow so that he doesn't have to -- he will not have to spend the weekend here, all right? Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we discussed it amongst us and agreed that the Prosecutor will not take as much time as initially envisaged. This witness will testify about the system, and this witness is very important for us. And we will be able to conclude our cross-examination only if the OTP shortens the direct examination. They promised to do so, and I thought it was important to say so for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would like to say that it will be co-counsel Gramsci Di Fazio, and he has assured me that he will try to streamline this direct testimony, and that is as a result of the discussion, I believe, with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, thank you. So we'll all meet tomorrow morning at 9.00 -- tomorrow afternoon. Tomorrow, the sitting is in the afternoon, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 10th day of February, 2005, at 2.15 p.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.54 p.m.,
